title: Nominative · Accusative · Dative
intro: The nominative marks the subject. The accusative often marks a direct object. The dative often marks a recipient. The genitive can express possession.
samples: The man is working. Der marks the subject.
I see the man. Den marks the direct object.
I help the man. Helfen takes the dative dem.
qs: Sehen takes an accusative object: den Mann.
Helfen takes the dative: der Frau.
Das Kind is the subject, so use the nominative.
The child receives the book: dem Kind.
Kennen takes an accusative object: den Lehrer.
Mit always takes the dative: mit dem Bus.
Possession calls for the genitive: des Kindes.
The recipient is dative: einer Frau.

title: Prepositions · Wo or wohin?
intro: Use the dative after mit, aus and zu, and the accusative after für. With a two-way preposition, distinguish a location from a destination.
samples: I’m in the city. Where? Dative.
I’m going into town. Where to? Accusative.
I’m taking the bus. Mit takes the dative.
qs: Mit dem Bus describes the means of transport.
Wohnen describes a location: in der Stadt.
The destination is in die Stadt.
Use zu for going to see a person: zu meinem Arzt.
Aus gives the place of origin and takes the dative.
The picture is already on the wall: an der Wand.
Ich hänge das Bild ___ die Wand.
The picture is being put on the wall: an die Wand.
